description_en: Aśikharatemple from the 14th-15th century built on top of a buried fountain.The monument is located in a field north of the village of Ukhāḍī.The temple is built on a small stone platform, atop a fountain. This fountain and the temple itself were accessible in the late 1960's, when Prayag Raj Sharma and Marc Gaborieau visited the place (Sharma 1972). It had to be unearthed by archaeologist Dominique Baudais in 2000. The fountain is currently buried, as well as parts of the temple.A pair of columns preceeds the entrance to the sanctum and creates a small porch (Skt.ardhamaṇḍapa). The porch supports a pediment containing a bas-relief carving of a couple on a horse. Eroded inscriptions are also observed on blocks of the pediment. The doorjambs are carved with motifs of volutes. The sanctum contained a large stoneyoni, on which aśivaliṅgamust have been installed, in 2000. Theyoniwas gone when the site was surveyed. The pinnacle is constituted of two stone discs (Skt. āmalaka)A stone memorial pillar is installed fifteen meters west of the temple (JUM0070-001).Suchśikharatemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 15th centuries (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates the dating of these monuments. Yet a line of eroded inscription on the pediment (below the riders' carving) appears to bear the date (ŚS) 1408 (1486 CE). Although the inscription may be much later than the monument itself, it provides a terminus ante quem for the temple's construction.
monument_assessment: Other, Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number JUM0070_I_001 Sources Sharma, P. R. 1972. Preliminary Study of the Art and Architecture of the Karnali Basin, West Nepal. Paris: CNRS.

historical_events.event_description: The pediment of the temple contains inscribed stone blocks. The inscriptions are very eroded, but it is possible to read the date 1408 of the Śaka era, which corresponds to 1486 CE.The inscription may record the construction of the temple or a later use of it.The inscription was first mentioned by Prayag Raj Sharma (1972).
